Kuparinen, K., Vakkilainen, E. and Tynjala, T. (2019). Biomass-based carbon capture and utilization in kraft pulp mills. Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change 24, 1213-1230. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11027-018-9833-9

Locators are printed journal page numbers (PDF page = printed - 1212). Two MillFlow-modelled reference mills (Mill A Nordic softwood integrated, natural-gas lime kiln; Mill B South American eucalyptus market pulp, oil lime kiln). Loaded: per-ADt typical CO2 ranges (recovery boiler biogenic, lime kiln fossil); per-mill recovery boiler CO2 and net steam per t dry solids; lime kiln fuel SEC derived from the MW labels in Figs 3-4 and CO2 split by the printed biogenic shares (64% / 55%); biomass boiler CO2 per BDt; MEA capture on the recovery boiler: energy-limited capture rates (21% / 32%), electricity and steam per t CO2 derived from Table 2 differences; generic MEA capture rate and 3.7 GJ/t regeneration heat (reprinted from Onarheim et al. 2015); lignin separation chemical inputs (flows). Not loaded: mill-wide balances, global potentials, CO2 cost figures (reprinted, no price year), utilization volumes (other-values). TRAPS: Table 2 prints Mill B base steam 860 t/h and base power 195 MW, contradicting Table 1 (660 t/h, 165 MW), Fig. 4 and the text (+22% steam, -10% power); Table 1 values used. No capex/opex in the paper.
